findings.specText: story-025 Review Failure Report 2026-08-31: "Re-derive the shortfall floor so a double-rounded-down ERC4626 delivery of `amount - 1` (or a routine haircut) does not revert autoAnnihilate." / "Because claimEnabled == false by default, autoAnnihilate is the only reward path, so the story's stated goal fails in production."
findings.specSource: story doc, '## Review Failure Report - 2026-08-31T23:02:24Z' (blocking [high]) and '## Autonomous Decisions — Round 3', Decision 1
findings.actualBehavior: EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE (2 raw units) + EXIT_ROUNDING_ALLOWANCE_BPS (1 bp) only absorb rounding-scale shortfall. ERC4626YieldStrategy does not override previewExitFor, so netFloor collapses to gross (AYieldStrategy capped identity); _disposeShares redeems the fee-free convertToShares(amount) while the vault's redeem returns assets net of fee. Any exit fee above 1 bp trips 'StableStaker: exit shortfall'. With claimEnabled false on deployment this is the only reward path.
findings.deviation: Round 3 satisfies the reviewer's criterion for rounding-scale shortfall only, and Decision 1 explicitly defers the fee case to a previewExitFor override in vault-RM that does not exist at the pinned commit cdd0743. The premise 'a case nobody has yet configured' is contestable: ERC4626YieldStrategy targets Tokemak-style autopools (reflax run-16, L-16 fee-blind NAV). The round-3 regression fixture (MockERC4626Vault = OZ reference ERC4626 + donation) charges no fee, so it cannot detect the residual.

findings.specText: CLAUDE.md as landed at 96d39ed: "...annihilates it against a slice of the caller's own booked principal, decrements userInfo.amount and poolInfo.totalStaked by the stable half..."
findings.specSource: lib/stable-staker/CLAUDE.md, section 'The claim gate and autoAnnihilate (story 025)', added afa7b80, uncorrected by 57eb02d/a961e10
findings.actualBehavior: src/StableStakerV2.sol:565-566 debits the GROSS: `user.amount -= gross; pool.totalStaked -= gross;`
findings.deviation: The headline paragraph states the round-1 net debit, which the story's own round-2 reopen identifies as the underflow bug ('if the cap stays on the net amount then user.amount -= stableNeeded underflows for exactly the user annihilating their whole position'). A later bullet in the same section states the correct gross semantics, so the document contradicts itself and the wrong version is the one a reader meets first.

findings.specText: story-025 Autonomous Decisions Round 2, Decision 4: "The probe is skipped when the strategy custodies nothing for the pool, because then there is no principal to annihilate against and the reward-outran-principal path still legitimately works — reporting `false` there would be the inconsistent answer."
findings.specSource: story doc, '## Autonomous Decisions — Round 2', Decision 4; round-2 checklist 'the view stays consistent with what the call will do'
findings.actualBehavior: The view early-returns true whenever strategy.principalOf(token, address(this)) == 0. But a staker can hold user.amount > 0 in that state (principal idle after a buffer-path relinquishPrincipal, or a strategy set before deposits route into it). Both previewExitFor implementations cap grossToRequest at the strategy's per-client ledger (AYieldStrategy.sol:579-581, ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:181-184), so grossQuote == 0 and line 557 reverts 'StableStaker: exit unavailable'.
findings.deviation: Decision 4 reasons that false would be the inconsistent answer; the code makes true the inconsistent answer. The view greenlights a button the transaction then refuses, which is the exact failure mode Decision 4 exists to prevent. Distinct from the >18-decimals cosmetic drift already carried forward from round 1.

findings.specText: CLAUDE.md round-3 carve-out: "The carve-out is the underwater path, which autoAnnihilate shares with withdraw and does not change: when _isUnderwater is true, _routeExit pays the whole request out of the idle balance plus relinquishPrincipal and returns the nominal amount without measuring anything." / round-2 checklist: "Tests — confirm the idle buffer is untouched across every case above"
findings.actualBehavior: _routeExit's underwater branch (:1184-1192) returns the nominal gross without touching the strategy, so received == gross. gross was grossed up by the strategy's slippage tolerance for a haircut that does not occur on this path, so surplus = gross - netWanted > 0 is safeTransferred to the caller out of the shared idle buffer, and relinquishPrincipal(token, gross) writes the strategy's booked principal down by the inflated figure.
findings.deviation: Not a value leak and not a Law-1 escalation: user.amount is debited by the same gross, and an equivalent withdraw already draws at par from the buffer. What is undisclosed is the rate — autoAnnihilate draws the tolerance-inflated gross from a scarce first-come buffer for a transaction that economically needs only netWanted, accelerating exhaustion against later stakers by the gross-up factor. No test covers autoAnnihilate against an underwater strategy, though round 3 corrected MockYieldStrategy.previewExitFor specifically so the case could be tested.

findings.specText: story-025 round-2 design item 2: "Cap the GROSS figure at the caller's own principal (user.amount) — not the net figure." / front-running analysis: "It is bounded: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy enforces minOut = idealUnderlying * (MAX_BPS - slippageToleranceBps) / MAX_BPS internally and reverts before autoAnnihilate ever sees the proceeds, so the extractable amount is capped at the tolerance..."
findings.specSource: story doc, '## Reopened — Round 2: Exit-Haircut Sizing', 'The agreed design' item 2 and 'Front-running analysis'
findings.actualBehavior: A second, unmodelled cap exists: both previewExitFor implementations cap grossToRequest at the strategy's per-client clientBalances[token][address(this)]. When it binds, grossQuote, gross, netFloor and netUsed all shrink below netWanted and the remainder is minted raw via `excess = excessBase + (netWanted - netUsed) * scale`. On ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy the cap binds structurally, because _acquireShares books the haircut creditedPrincipal rather than the nominal deposit, so clientBalances is permanently below the pool's nominal totalStaked.
findings.deviation: The story bounds the raw-mint path by the AMM slippage tolerance. The real bound is min(user.amount, clientBalances[token][staker]); the second term is neither user-controllable (so not an attack vector) nor bounded by the tolerance. Conservation still holds — owed in equals annihilated + raw-minted + carried dust — so no antimatter is created beyond what the caller was owed. Documentation fix, not a code fix.

candidatesDeclined: excess raw-mint loophole around the closed claim gate — quantity equals what claim() would mint, no dilution of the unbacked-phUSD backing set; the gate is stated repeatedly as UX, never a security boundary. The V2 Antimatter/unbacked-phUSD carve-out was applied and does not bite: there is no over-payment, only a change of delivery form.

self-sandwiching the exit to widen the raw-mint path — analysed in the story, bounded by the strategy's own minOut, costed at a real AMM round trip. F-05 corrects the statement of the bound but the second cap is protocol-level, not caller-set.
underwater buffer draw (F-04) — caller is debited the same gross they receive; an equivalent withdraw already draws at par from the same buffer.
